metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: The proposed method takes preprocessed video data as inputs. Vehicle locations are extracted from traffic video frames and reformed as position matrices to represent traffic states. Three consecutive frames are used as observation input, with one observation sized 4x512 pixels after down-sampling.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Explicitly states 'available from the corresponding author upon request'.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used to calibrate simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors. It includes 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in the mainline and at the on-ramp.
nodes_source.size_estimate: 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: General 'Data Availability' section states all data is 'available from the corresponding author upon request'.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations from video frames
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Identifies vehicle locations (as points x,y) from raw traffic video frames. The control area size is unspecified in terms of absolute values, but represented as X x Y.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, no specific algorithms or tools mentioned for location extraction beyond the concept, and dimensions are symbolic.

nodes_process.node_name: Represent traffic state as position matrix
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m_t E R^X x Y;
nodes_process.description: Converts vehicle location points and signal states into a position matrix (m_t), where non-zero entries (constants Uv, UG, UR) indicate vehicle presence or signal state at position (x, y). All other elements are zero.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, method fully specified with formulas (Eq 3, 4, 5), but constant values for signals/vehicles are not specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: After zooming and down-sampling, the size of one observation is 4x512 in pixels.
nodes_process.description: Reduces the input dimensions of the position matrices for computational efficiency, resulting in a down-sampled observation size of 4x512 pixels. This step aims to maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, target output size mentioned but specific down-sampling algorithm (e.g. method, kernel) not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s_t: S_t = {m_{t-(N-1)},..., m_t}.
nodes_process.description: Stacks position matrices from N consecutive time steps to form the complete traffic state representation. The total number of consecutive frames stacked is 3.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, the formula and the number of stacked frames are explicitly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: Designs a deep Q-network architecture for approximating the optimal action-value function, consisting of three convolutional layers and two fully connected layers (one for Q-value, one for speed+queue prediction). It contains about 2 million weights.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all architecture parameters detailed in Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r_t after action a_t is defined by the following: r_t = \mu v_t + \omega q_t, \mu > 0, \omega < 0
nodes_process.description: Defines the reward for the DRL agent as a weighted sum of the average speed in the merging area and the average queue length at the on-ramp during time steps t and t+1.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, reward formula and all weighting parameters specified in text and Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1. The ramp meter takes new action with the e-greedy strategy
nodes_process.description: Trains the Deep Q-network using Q-learning, experience replay, a target network, Adam optimizer, and an epsilon-greedy strategy. Training involves multitask learning for concurrent prediction of speed and queue length over 10^6 frames.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, most parameters from Table 1 specified, but two different total training duration units are mentioned with slight ambiguity.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao
nodes_process.description: Configures a microscopic traffic simulation environment using SUMO, modeling a freeway network connecting Qingdao and Huangdao. Simulation parameters for driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, main tool and key parameters stated, but full details for calibrating 'driving behaviors' not given.

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase... r_k = r_{k-1} + K_R[o_k - \hat{o}] - K_P[o_{k-1} - o_k]
nodes_process.description: Implements the Proportional-Integral-based ALINEA (PI-ALINEA) method, a rule-based approach adjusting ramp metering rates based on downstream occupancy, using a fixed green phase and a variable red phase.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, formula and all parameters (KR, KP, desired occupancy, green phase length) explicitly stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate DRL and baseline performance in simulation
nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the performance of the proposed DRL method, PI-ALINEA, and a no-control scenario through 20 simulation experiments, each initialized with different random seeds. Metrics include travel times, speed distribution, queue lengths, and traffic flows.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, number of experiments stated, but specific random seeds used for initialization are not provided.

nodes_process.node_name: Conduct perturbation analysis on input data
nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: Divides the control area into 8 subareas and evaluates the DRL controller's performance by removing information from each subarea sequentially, using 20 simulation experiments with perturbed data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, number of subareas and experiments given, but precise method of 'removing information' from subareas not detailed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: This figure shows the convergence curves of the deep Q-learning model during training, illustrating the progression of episode reward and mean travel time over 1 million frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Input video data for DRL training not openly available. DRL parameters and training process are largely described, but specific raw simulation logs are missing.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9: Vehicle travel times in the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: This figure presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 quantiles of vehicle travel times in the mainline for three scenarios (no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL) over time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Empirical and video input data not accessible. Simulation setup and control policies are detailed, but full replication requires precise SUMO model & data.

nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Empirical and video input data not accessible. Simulation setup and control policies are detailed, but full replication requires precise SUMO model & data.
